Write a portable judge audit artifact

Source: R/integrations.R
write_audit.Rd

Writes either the Markdown evidence report or a versioned JSON summary. The JSON artifact does not automatically serialize x$items; it contains aggregate evidence, policy checks, and provenance.

Usage

write_audit(
  x,
  path,
  bias = NULL,
  stability = NULL,
  policy = NULL,
  format = c("json", "md"),
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A yourhonor_calibration object.

path

Output file path. An existing file is never replaced unless overwrite = TRUE, so a re-run cannot silently clobber an earlier audit.

bias

Optional bias evidence.

stability

Optional stability evidence.

policy

Optional acceptance policy.

format

"json" or "md".

overwrite

Replace an existing file at path? Defaults to FALSE.

Value

path, invisibly.

Privacy

Calibration item rows are omitted from JSON. Caller-supplied provenance is serialized verbatim, however, so do not place secrets or raw item content in provenance fields.

JSON schema (yourhonor.audit.v1)

The JSON artifact is written at full numeric precision: doubles carry 17 significant digits, so every value round-trips exactly (a reader may see 0.94999999999999996 for 0.95). That is the precision of the stored doubles, not of the estimates: irrCAC rounds each agreement and stability coefficient to five decimals, so every estimate (and stability's gwet_agreement) and every bootstrap draw sits on that grid, and the bootstrap bounds interpolated between draws are no more precise. conf_low_exact is computed from irrCAC's unrounded observed and chance agreement and is capped at the rounded estimate (and at the bound of the perfect samples it can be corrected into; see agreement()). Every absent value is null: an NA and an R NULL are indistinguishable to a reader, but neither ever appears as {} or is dropped. Fields that are vectors by contract are always JSON arrays, even when they hold one value. Top-level members:

  • schema_version: "yourhonor.audit.v1".

  • created_at: UTC timestamp in RFC 3339 form, e.g. "2026-01-31T12:00:00Z".

  • decision: the overall assessment (PASS, FAIL, INDETERMINATE, or NOT_ASSESSED).

  • audit_id: string or null.

  • policy: null, or an object with one member per acceptance_policy() argument. A null coefficient means the calibration's Gwet coefficient, which the agreement_<coefficient> check names. required_probes is an array; min_recall and min_precision are a number when global or an object keyed by class name when class-specific; unset thresholds are null.

  • checks: array of objects, one per policy check, with check, status, value (the number compared with threshold, null when unavailable: the observed value, or for an interval check the bound assessed, which for a bias probe's flip-rate and directional checks counts every unscored item against the probe over n_input: as a flip for the flip rate, towards the worse direction for the directional rate), op (the comparison the check encodes: ">=", "<=", "lower >=", "upper <=", or "="), a numeric threshold, and reason. Without a policy the single placeholder check has null op and threshold.

  • calibration: n_input, n_items, n_excluded, n_consensus_ties, n_judge_abstentions, judge_abstention_rate, judge_abstention_conf_low, judge_abstention_conf_high, scale, weights, conf_level, n_boot, seed (scalars); label_levels and coefficients (arrays); agreement, confusion, confusion_metrics, human_reliability, and per_rater_agreement (arrays of row objects mirroring the tibble columns; human_reliability and per_rater_agreement are null for a single rater). confusion holds one row per reference-by-judge cell, empty cells included, with the reference label, the judge label, the count n, and its share prop, so a reader can rebuild the matrix in label_levels order.

  • bias: null, or audit_id plus results, an array of row objects with the columns of the bias tibble.

  • stability: null, or the scalar summary fields of a yourhonor_stability object (n_items, n_items_scored, n_runs, pairwise_disagreement*, gwet_*, missing_rate, *_ci_reliable), label_levels (array), and provenance.

  • provenance: the calibration provenance. The keys input_cols, human_cols, label_levels, and content_cols are always arrays, even when they were supplied by the caller and hold one value; created_at is RFC 3339 UTC like the top-level field, and adapter fields left NULL (id_col, audit_id) are present as null.
